other_failure_modes.name: Improper test set imputation

other_failure_modes.name: Unhandled missing categorical values
other_failure_modes.description: The agent explicitly restricts median imputation to numeric columns, leaving missing values in categorical columns unhandled. This will cause downstream transformers (like OrdinalEncoder) or the neural network to fail.

other_failure_modes.name: Categoricals treated as continuous in neural network
other_failure_modes.description: The agent applies OrdinalEncoder to categorical columns and feeds the resulting arbitrary integers directly into a Multi-Layer Perceptron alongside numeric features. Without embedding layers or one-hot encoding, the network will incorrectly interpret these categorical indices as continuous magnitudes.

other_failure_modes.name: Failure to preserve test IDs
other_failure_modes.description: The agent generates a generic sequence for the submission file's 'id' column instead of extracting and preserving the actual IDs from the test set. This will cause submission scoring to fail if the expected IDs are non-sequential or specific identifiers.

other_failure_modes.name: Including ID column as a feature

summary: The agent builds a well-regularised PyTorch MLP for the regression task but makes several critical data processing errors. It imputes missing values before the train/validation split, uses test set statistics to impute the test set, and fails to handle missing values in categorical columns entirely. Additionally, categorical features are passed to the neural network as ordinal integers without embeddings, no feature engineering is performed, and the final submission fails to preserve true test IDs.
